extracted.intended_audience: Registered apprenticeship stakeholders: program sponsors, employers, State Apprenticeship Agencies (SAAs), Office of Apprenticeship (OA), workforce partners, and policymakers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and proposed regulatory criteria for establishing, operating, and overseeing registered apprenticeship programs under proposed revisions to 29 CFR part 29, including quality hallmarks, governance, accountability, data collection, and a new CTE-aligned apprenticeship model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicia of a registered apprenticeship
rubrics_metrics.description: Apprentices entering into a registered apprenticeship program share several common indicia: they enter into a paid job from the outset; they receive progressive wage increases reflecting their progress through a training regimen developed by industry stakeholders; they participate in related instruction informing them of the theoretical or academic concepts that underpin the work processes and competencies critical to success in their chosen career; and they ultimately develop a set of portable, in-demand job skills culminating with the awarding of a nationally recognized certificate of completion of a registered apprenticeship that benefit them throughout their careers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These indicia function as practical hallmarks for identifying and designing registered apprenticeship programs: guarantee paid employment from start, structure progressive wages tied to training milestones, include related classroom instruction, and award a nationally recognized credential upon successful completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: On-the-job training and related instruction as definitional elements
rubrics_metrics.description: As an earn-and-learn workforce development strategy, registered apprenticeship combines on-the-job training with related (classroom) instruction, blending the practical and theoretical aspects of training for highly skilled occupations. On-the-job training and related instruction are critical, definitional elements of registered apprenticeship that provide practical benefits to both employers and apprentices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs must incorporate both supervised practical job training and related classroom/theoretical instruction; these components are used to develop competency and to measure apprentice proficiency over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of apprenticeship must align with minimum quality and content requirements (29 CFR part 29)
rubrics_metrics.description: The part 29 regulations prescribe minimum quality and content requirements with respect to a program's standards of apprenticeship and its apprenticeship agreements; establish procedures concerning the registration, cancellation, and deregistration of apprenticeship programs; and set forth a mechanism for the recognition of SAAs as Registration Agencies authorized to register and oversee registered apprenticeship programs in a State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any program seeking registration for Federal purposes must develop program standards aligned with the regulatory minimums (currently codified at 29 CFR 29.5 and proposed updates at 29 CFR 29.8). These standards govern program structure, apprenticeship agreements, and procedural interactions with OA/SAAs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal employment opportunity requirements (29 CFR part 30)
rubrics_metrics.description: A companion regulation, at 29 CFR part 30, implements the NAA by setting forth minimum EEO requirements that registered apprenticeship programs must follow in order to obtain and maintain registration status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs must comply with part 30 EEO provisions as a condition of registration; EEO compliance is part of the program quality and legal baseline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation and improvement of apprenticeship quality and working conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Foremost among the Department's goals is the preservation of quality throughout all registered apprenticeship programs. The Department seeks to improve the quality of apprenticeship training and the quality of working conditions for apprentices, and to further promote DEIA principles and goals throughout the National Apprenticeship System.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality improvements include strengthening training content and workplace protections, incorporating DEIA, and ensuring apprentices are safeguarded in terms of safety, welfare, and equitable treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for apprentices against restrictive provisions and unreasonable costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department proposes quality improvements ... such as proposed prohibitions on non-compete and non-disclosure provisions in apprenticeship agreements between sponsors and apprentices and enhanced protections against unreasonable participation costs for apprentices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apprenticeship agreements should not contain non-compete or overbroad non-disclosure clauses that restrict labor market mobility; sponsors must avoid imposing unreasonable costs of participation on apprentices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improved accountability and assignment of responsibilities for participating employers
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department proposes several accountability enhancements throughout this proposal, including a clearer assignment of responsibilities for employers that participate in a registered apprenticeship program (but do not serve as a program sponsor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear delineation of duties between sponsors and other participating employers is required to support program oversight and apprentice protections; accountability mechanisms should be codified to ensure compliance and roles clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governance reforms clarifying roles of OA, SAAs, and State Apprenticeship Councils
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department is also proposing reforms to the governance structure and the relationship between OA and SAAs, including clarifying the respective roles and duties of SAAs and State Apprenticeship Councils.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules should articulate the responsibilities and interplay between federal OA and State-level SAAs/Councils to increase transparency, consistency, and effective oversight across jurisdictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishing a registered CTE apprenticeship model with tailored baseline requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department proposes to establish regulations for an additional model of apprenticeship that aligns State-approved CTE programs ... This model, defined as registered CTE apprenticeship, would deliver the industry-specific portions of the paid on-the-job training and related instruction components of registered apprenticeship through a State-approved CTE program. The proposed baseline requirements for registered CTE apprenticeship programs would account for this target population and the increased alignment with educational institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registered CTE apprenticeship programs should be structured to serve secondary and postsecondary students or early-career individuals, with pathways to employment, postsecondary education, or subpart A registered apprenticeship, potentially offering advanced standing or credit. Baseline regulatory requirements should reflect these educational alignments and target-population needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform national approach and Department authority over occupation suitability determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department seeks to establish a more uniform and nationally applicable approach to system governance ... including by retaining the ultimate authority and responsibility to make determinations regarding an occupation's suitability for registered apprenticeship training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A consistent national framework for occupation suitability and program governance is intended to reduce multistate variability and aid employers operating nationally; the Department will retain final decision-making authority on occupation suitability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhanced data collection and a modern data framework with uniform elements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department seeks to establish a truly national and comprehensive database ... update requirements regarding the collection and maintenance of data for program stakeholders. The proposed rule also presents new data elements for collection ... requiring program sponsors to provide data on the interim credentials or other industry-recognized certifications offered through their programs and requiring that applications for a determination on an occupation's suitability for registered apprenticeship training include information relating to the career wage profile of the subject occupation. Additionally, the Department would collect information from sponsors on pre-apprenticeship program engagement and placement ... prioritize collecting information on both postsecondary academic credit and industry-recognized credentials ... in addition to their acquisition of Certificates of Completion of registered apprenticeship programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data collection should be standardized and disaggregable (e.g., by race/ethnicity, industry, occupation, state/national) to enable performance accountability, equity analysis, and informed policy decisions. Required elements include interim credentials, career wage profiles, pre-apprenticeship placements, postsecondary credits, industry credentials, and Certificates of Completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance accountability, transparency, and outcomes focus
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department believes this is an opportunity to orient the National Apprenticeship System around increased performance accountability, transparency, and a focus on outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory and data systems should support evaluation of program performance and equitable outcomes, enabling OA and SAAs to use data-driven insights for oversight, improvement, and communication of apprenticeship value.

rubrics_metrics.name: National occupational and program tools to support onboarding and program development
rubrics_metrics.description: In the proposed regulation, the Department introduces and defines the purpose of new products to support the development of new registered apprenticeship programs. These products—National Occupational Standards for Apprenticeship, National Guidelines for Apprenticeship Standards, and National Program Standards for Apprenticeship—would feature ample opportunities for industry to provide input and feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adoption of standardized national tools (standards, guidelines, program templates) developed with industry input is intended to ease onboarding, ensure quality consistency, and help new sectors adopt apprenticeship models.

rubrics_metrics.name: System modernization and use of technology for administrative functions and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department's vision for a modern system also includes an acceleration of its ongoing efforts to leverage advancements in technology to improve its internal systems and data analysis capabilities; modernize and strengthen the reporting tools available to registered apprenticeship program sponsors, SAAs, and other stakeholders; and move the system's administrative functions fully online.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs and Registration Agencies should adopt streamlined, digital administrative processes and reporting tools to improve data quality, reporting timeliness, and stakeholder access to systems and insights.

rubrics_metrics.name: OA oversight, technical assistance, and program review to identify quality hallmarks and address persistent issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Ongoing oversight of the National Apprenticeship System conducted by OA's staff ... including technical assistance and support provided to registered apprenticeship program sponsors, potential sponsors ... as well as formal reviews of individual programs, internal processes, and apprenticeship's place in national workforce development, has ... been an important source of data that underpins this proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OA's review and technical assistance activities inform identification of program quality hallmarks, persistent issues, and gaps. Effective oversight should include proactive assistance, program reviews, and use of findings to improve regulatory standards and onboarding resources.
